payload.question: Do current TESS archive values distinguish resolved TOIs (CP and FP) from unresolved planet candidates (PC and APC)? Provisional, not locked. Preregistered T1 shift check (docs/coordination/TESS_RESOLUTION_SHIFT_PREREGISTRATION.md): a catalog-snapshot measurement, not vetting accuracy.

claims.quote_span: We present 2241 exoplanet candidates identified with data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) during its two-year prime mission.
claims.text: The TOI catalog that the TESS archive dispositions (CP, FP, PC, APC) come from was first described as a release of planet candidates found in TESS prime-mission data. This is background on where the catalog comes from. It is not evidence about whether archive values separate resolved TOIs from unresolved ones.

claims.quote_span: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) will search for planets transiting bright and nearby stars.
claims.text: TESS was designed to look for planets transiting bright, nearby stars. This defines the population that TOIs are drawn from. It is mission background, not a finding about how dispositions shift.

payload.claim: AI-generated hypothesis, not a finding. In the current TESS TOI archive snapshot, resolved TOIs (CP and FP) and unresolved candidates (PC and APC) have different distributions of archive values, with resolved TOIs skewed toward brighter host stars (lower TESS mag) and higher transit SNR or depth. The plausible reason is that follow-up resources go first to targets that are easier to observe. The cited evidence (arXiv:2103.12538, arXiv:1406.0151) is background on where the catalog and population come from. It does not support this claim directly.
payload.falsifier: H1 is falsified if the T1 shift is below the preregistered threshold, its confidence interval includes zero, or it points the wrong way (unresolved candidates brighter or higher-SNR) on every preregistered archive value. Results that only show up in values that were not preregistered, or that change with the snapshot date, do not count as support.
payload.prediction: In the frozen catalog snapshot, the preregistered T1 shift check in docs/coordination/TESS_RESOLUTION_SHIFT_PREREGISTRATION.md finds a shift between resolved and unresolved groups that exceeds the preregistered threshold and has a confidence interval excluding zero, in the expected direction, on at least one preregistered archive value (e.g., TESS mag or SNR/depth). This describes the catalog only. It says nothing about vetting accuracy.

payload.label: UNCERTAIN
payload.search_scope: Run live-exo-9. No literature search tool was available, so I did not search ADS, arXiv or Google Scholar. I checked only the two cited sources against the claim. arXiv:2103.12538 (TOI catalog release) is the closest prior work I can name: it describes the catalog and TFOP follow-up but does not directly test the claim. arXiv:1406.0151 (TESS mission design) is population background only and is left out of prior_art. It is widely assumed in the community that follow-up favors bright, high-SNR targets, so a clean NOVEL label is unlikely. I could not identify a specific paper that measures CP/FP vs PC/APC distribution shifts in TESS mag or SNR in a frozen snapshot, so I can't call it KNOWN either. Next step: search ADS for TOI disposition completeness and TFOP follow-up selection-bias studies. This verdict is a search result, not proof of novelty.

payload.falsifier: H1 is falsified if, on every preregistered archive value, the T1 shift is below the preregistered threshold, or its bootstrap CI includes zero, or it points the wrong way (unresolved TOIs brighter or higher SNR). payload.metric: T1 resolution-shift statistic as defined in docs/coordination/TESS_RESOLUTION_SHIFT_PREREGISTRATION.md, computed on each preregistered archive value (TESS mag, SNR/depth). The sign is set so that positive means resolved (CP+FP) TOIs are brighter or have higher SNR/depth than unresolved (PC+APC) TOIs. A bootstrap confidence interval comes from 200 resamples. This is a measurement of the catalog snapshot, not of vetting accuracy.

The permutation test is skipped. The same T1 shift check plus the permutation test and a larger bootstrap (n=1000), for a stronger null calibration. Not preregistered for this run.

The prior of 0.55 leaves the outcome open, so one cheap run still tells us a lot. The permutation test adds little beyond the bootstrap CI for a test of direction plus CI. The planner had no file-read tools, so it did not read the preregistration's exact threshold, snapshot ID or seed. data_ver and seeds must be taken from the script output and checked against the preregistration before RUN_STARTED is treated as complete. The predicted mean and sd are an AI-generated prior on the sign-oriented shift, not a measured value.

payload.notes: The gate ran once and an output file timestamped from this run was written. Its stdout (about 102k chars) went to a tool-results file that was not read, so the gate's approval text was not confirmed directly. The permutation test was skipped (permutation_null_primary_arm=null). The script measures how well a classifier separates resolved from unresolved TOIs using all 39 fields together (multivariate OOF AUC). It does not give a separate shift or direction for st_tmag, SNR or depth, so H1's directional claim (resolved = brighter / higher SNR) was not tested. A shift was found in this catalog snapshot; it does not measure vetting accuracy. This is a preliminary result, not benchmark evidence.

payload.limits: [AI-generated analyst conclusion; preliminary] Judged against the preregistered AUC rule (AUC > 0.5 with a 95% bootstrap CI that excludes 0.5). The grouped out-of-fold ROC AUC for {CP,FP} vs {PC,APC} on 39 numeric fields meets that rule (n_rows=7427: 2127 resolved, 5300 unresolved, 7143 hosts). Per-seed AUC ranged from 0.7595 to 0.7627. METRIC MISMATCH: PREDICTION_COMMITTED described a sign-oriented per-feature shift statistic (mean 0.15, sd 0.15), but the run measured multivariate AUC. That prior was never scored, and H1's directional claim (resolved TOIs are brighter or have higher SNR/depth) was NOT tested. The permutation null was skipped (permutation_null_primary_arm=null). The bootstrap used n=200, not the preregistered 2000. The gate's approval text was not read directly. The FA-as-resolved sensitivity arm gives a similar result: 0.7655 [0.7546, 0.7750]. The with-timestamps arm is higher, 0.7992 [0.7869, 0.8119], which suggests time-related fields carry extra signal. It is not primary evidence. This shows only that classes in the current catalog snapshot can be separated (retrieved 2026-10-04, sha256 485a05d6…). It is not a triage-time shift, not vetting accuracy, not causal, and not benchmark evidence.

payload.next: E2: rerun the primary arm at the preregistered settings (2000 bootstrap resamples plus the permutation null) and record the gate approval in the ledger. In the same run, add the preregistered per-feature directional test on st_tmag, SNR and depth: grouped by host, sign-oriented so that positive means resolved TOIs are brighter or have higher SNR/depth, each with a bootstrap CI. Score these against the committed falsifier, which requires the preregistered threshold, a CI that excludes zero, and the correct sign on every value. Keep the with-timestamps arm as a snapshot-dependence diagnostic only.
